of Villa Magni in May and June, a tension that ‘developed to the point of hallucinations in
Shelley and Jane, and to near-hysteria in Mary’ (for S.’s vision of a child in the sea on 6 May

her miscarriage, S.’s hallucinations, and Jane Williams’s strange vision of S. on the terrace at
Villa Magni, in her letter to Maria Gisborne, 15 August 1822, Mary L i 245–6). According to
Edward Williams’s journal, during the night of 23 June S. ‘sees spirits and alarms the whole
